title: 36-Round Differential Security of a Generalized Feistel Cipher
summary: A 9-round impossible truncated differential is known, while whether 36 rounds prevent truncated and impossible differentials in the single-tweak setting remains conjectural.

formal_statement.body: For the generalized Feistel cipher construction used for efficient prime-field masking, a 9-round impossible truncated differential is derived, and the unresolved task is to prove or refute whether 36 rounds suffice to prevent truncated and impossible differential attacks in the single-tweak setting.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of a generalized Feistel block cipher for efficient prime-field masking.
parameters: 9 rounds: length of the derived impossible truncated differential
36 rounds: conjectured round count for preventing truncated and impossible differential attacks
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that 36 rounds suffice to prevent truncated and impossible differential attacks in the single-tweak setting.

citations.label: Generalized Feistel Ciphers for Efficient Prime Field Masking

progress.summary: The paper derives a 9-round impossible truncated differential and explicitly conjectures that 36 rounds suffice to prevent truncated and impossible differentials in the single-tweak setting.
